topic: Species, Genus, Family, Order, Class, Phylum and Kingdom
title: Mango to Housefly: The 7 Ranks Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
A mango, a grain of wheat, a housefly and you: four living things, and each one has a full address in biology, seven lines long. Diya sees a housefly land on a mango in her kitchen and asks how close these living things really are.

We walk the mango up the ladder of ranks, step by step, inside a live diagram of groups within groups: species Mangifera indica, genus Mangifera, family Anacardiaceae, order Sapindales, class Dicotyledonae, division Angiospermae, kingdom Plantae. A labelled housefly shows why it sits in Insecta, Arthropoda and Diptera. We compare mango and wheat (dicot vs monocot) to find where they split, then fill in the full address of a human from NCERT Table 1.1. Then the exam trap about Diptera and Muscidae, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 7 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Four living things, one seven-line address
0:26 The seven main ranks: groups inside groups
0:46 The mango climbs the ladder, rank by rank
1:48 The housefly, labelled: Insecta, Arthropoda, Diptera
2:21 Mango vs wheat: dicot vs monocot + pause and think
3:12 Worked example: the full address of a human
3:44 Exam trap: Diptera is the order, not the family
4:11 Practice question (NEET pattern)
4:37 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Binomial Nomenclature and Scientific Naming Rules. The same fish has a different name in every language: so which name do scientists use?
